name: Archer Technologies

Bain Capital Ventures supported Archer as they enhanced their business model and created a hybrid sales team that resulted in a more efficient sales process. Bain Capital Ventures also helped develop new channels. Through board participation and serving as acting CFO, Bain Capital Ventures provided guidance throughout the sale process by negotiating terms of the sale. Archer Technologies was acquired by EMC 15 months after the initial investment and now operates as part of RSA, the Security Division of EMC.

name: Lala
outcome: Lala was acquired by Apple, Inc. on December 2009.
worked_with: Bain Capital Ventures led the Series A round of financing and helped Lala with strategy development. Like many businesses, Lala realized that its original business model, a CD-swapping exchange, needed to evolve. The music industry was undergoing profound and rapid change, and Bain Capital Ventures helped Lala develop a strategy and new business model to effectively participate in the shift and eventually become an enabler. Bain Capital Ventures helped execute the first step of the new strategy by making an introduction to Warner Music, a company part of the Bain Capital private equity portfolio. Lala signed a deal with Warner Music to access Warner Music’s entire library and received an investment from Warner Music. Shortly after the deal, Lala secured rights to all the other major music labels and publishers. Lala also struck an agreement with Google. In late 2009, in what was considered a transformational acquisition Lala was acquired by Apple, Inc and Bain Capital Ventures assisted in the negotiations during the sale.

name: Liberty Dialysis
outcome: Liberty Dialysis was acquired by Fresenius Medical in February 2012.
worked_with: Bain Capital Ventures seeded and co-founded Liberty Dialysis alongside management in 2002 and has been involved continuously with the company since that time. As Liberty has grown and required different types of financing, Bain Capital Ventures has helped the company meet its financing goals. In addition to investing in subsequent equity rounds, Bain Capital Ventures helped Liberty raise debt to finance the opening of de novo clinics, as well as to complete M&A. More recently, Bain Capital Ventures assisted in the company’s merger with Renal Advantage. The combined company is now the third largest dialysis provider in the US and serves over 19,000 patients in 32 states.

name: LinkedIn
outcome: IPO on 5/19/11 (NYSE: LNKD)
worked_with: In 2008, Bain Capital Ventures and our affiliates provided a substantial investment to LinkedIn that allowed the company to further expand its growth efforts and gave the business the needed financial resources to continue its investments in product, sales, and technology. Over the past several years, Bain Capital Ventures actively participated in the LinkedIn board, was involved in the hiring of key team members, and made many customer introductions across the board Bain Capital network. Over the investment period, LinkedIn grew from approximately 125 employees and 17 million members to more than 1000 employees and 100 million members worldwide. In May of 2011, LinkedIn completed a successful IPO of more than $300 million on the NYSE.

name: m-Qube
outcome: m-Qube was acquired by VeriSign in May 2006.
worked_with: Bain Capital Ventures led the series A funding of m-Qube in May 2002 and was instrumental in making a number of early customer introductions, assisting in team building, and providing years of strategic guidance. The Bain Capital name added credibility in early negotiations with wireless carriers who wanted the comfort of knowing that m-Qube had a strong financial foundation. Several Bain Capital Ventures employees lent a hand in diligencing acquisition candidates over the years. Perhaps most importantly, Bain Capital Ventures displayed even-keeled board support during both the early tough times as well as during the later hyper growth phase of the company. m-Qube won numerous industry awards and launched many industry firsts such as the first mobile couponing program, cross carrier premium SMS campaigns, and off carrier deck content delivery. The business was named the fastest growing company in New England in 2005 growing at over 1200%.

name: SolarWinds
outcome: IPO on 5/20/09 (NYSE: SWI)
worked_with: At the time of the Bain Capital Ventures investment, SolarWinds was at a pivotal point in the company’s history - the company was looking to find the right investment partner to help further accelerate its growth. The first step was building up the management team. Bain Capital Ventures helped SolarWinds select and recruit a CEO and Executive Management team. In addition, Bain Capital Ventures helped SolarWinds relocate to Austin, Texas to have access to talent to build out its management team and board. As the company grew, Bain Capital Ventures helped SolarWinds reorient it sales model from an inbound approach to an outbound strategy. SolarWinds utilized its brand recognition to expand into new product areas. Bain Capital Ventures also provided introductions and assistance on multiple acquisitions to supplement the company’s platform before becoming public. As part of the IPO process, SolarWinds leveraged the Bain Capital network for market and financing insight. Bain Capital Ventures helped SolarWinds complete a highly successful IPO on the NYSE in May 2009 in the amount of ~$150M. Today, Bain Capital Ventures serves on the SolarWinds Board of Directors and as Chairman of the Compensation Committee. At the time of the initial Bain Capital Ventures investment, SolarWinds had ~23,000 corporate customers. At the time of its IPO, the SolarWinds customer base had grown to ~60,000. Today, SolarWinds has over 95,000 customers.
